description: Evaluation scenarios for the loop-and-postprocess skill (audio pipeline post stage).

scenarios.query: The chiptune loop I generated has a few seconds of silence at the end and the loop point clicks. Make it a proper seamless loop.
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/post_process.py with the asset slug rather than hand-building ffmpeg commands
Passes --candidate (or points at stages.generate.selected) instead of guessing when the asset has more than one candidate
Explains that the trailing silence is trimmed to the last fully contentful bar, so the loop may come out shorter than the requested bar count
Reports the resulting bar count and duration from stages.post.loopProcessing rather than assuming the requested length
Tells the user to hear the wrap by playing the file twice in a row or looping it in engine, and does not treat the recorded seamRatio as proof on its own

scenarios.query: I asked for 18 bars and post_process only gave me 15. Re-run it until I get all 18.
expected_behavior: Explains that ACE-Step's planner ended the song around bar 15 and the remaining bars are silence, so the 15-bar loop is the correct result
Does not re-run the post stage repeatedly, which is deterministic and would produce the same cut
Offers the real fix if 18 bars are genuinely needed: regenerate with a different seed or a shorter requirement.durationSeconds, not more post-processing
Points at the recorded contentEndSeconds / bars figures as the evidence
Does not silently pad the loop with silence or stretch it to reach 18 bars

scenarios.query: Normalize this vocal track to -16 LUFS and give me an ogg. It was made with MiniMax.
expected_behavior: Runs post_process.py and lets requirement.targetLufs and requirement.formats drive the run instead of inventing flags

Reports this candidate's own measured input true peak from stages.post.normalize.measuredInput rather than reciting a remembered figure (one earlier MiniMax take measured +0.11 dBTP, which is an example, not this file's value)
Explains that MiniMax candidates arrive unnormalized and can sit above 0 dBTP, which is what the -1.0 dBTP ceiling exists to pull back before the 16-bit and Vorbis exports are written
Verifies the measured output loudness and true peak from stages.post.normalize rather than assuming the normalization hit the target
Mentions that the ogg may read a fraction of a dB above the ceiling as normal encoder overshoot, and that only a reading at or above 0 dBTP is a failure
Does not use requirement.bpm for bar snapping on a MiniMax take without the user having measured the tempo

scenarios.query: Trim the silence off this door creak sound effect and export it for Unity.
expected_behavior: Recognises the asset as a one-shot (requirement.loop false) and does not apply bar snapping or a loop crossfade
Explains that the trailing trim keeps 0.2 s past the last contentful window so the decay is not clipped, and that a short leading pre-roll under 0.5 s is left alone
Points at post/<slug>.wav (16-bit PCM) as the file the engine loads, and master.wav as the float archive copy
Checks the exported file for clipping and for the expected duration before reporting success
Does not suggest re-generating the sound effect when the fix is a trim

scenarios.query: Everything in this project has to be 44.1 kHz, but the ACE-Step tracks came out at 48k. Convert them.
expected_behavior: Uses post_process.py --target-rate 44100 rather than a separate conversion step after export
Explains that the resample happens once, at the end, with soxr precision 28, because 44.1 <-> 48 kHz is not an integer ratio
Notes that the float master.wav stays at the source rate and only the exports are converted
Confirms that a bar-exact loop stays bar-exact after the conversion, by checking the exported duration
Does not resample the candidate before processing or chain two conversions
